turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil asked Sandip if he was truly so blind to the reality of the situation, and if he was aware of the consequences of his actions.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if his warnings were a result of genuine concern for the zamindars, or if there was another reason behind them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was starting to enjoy these theatrics, where Nikhil would strut around, warning him of imaginary dangers, and that it was almost as if Nikhil was auditioning for a role in a melodrama.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that he was not indulging in theatrics, but was compelled by a sense of duty to warn Sandip of the impending danger, and that he would not be swayed by Sandip's ridicule.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil to clarify what specific actions he was advising the zamindars to take in response to the potential threat from the Mussulmans, and what measures he was proposing to take to mitigate the danger.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was a master weaver of tales, but his fabric was thinning, and his knots were unraveling, and that Nikhil's warnings were nothing but a desperate attempt to salvage his own tattered reputation.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant remarks only served to underscore the gravity of the situation and that he would not be swayed by Sandip's attempts to belittle his warnings.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil how he proposed to verify the credibility of the rumors about the Mussulmans and what evidence he had to support his claims of an impending attack.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had considered the possibility that the rumors were being spread by Nikhil himself, to further his own agenda and justify his own inflated sense of importance.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the matter was too grave to be treated as a mere fabrication, and that he had credible sources that confirmed the rumors about the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the possibility that the rumors were being spread by the local villagers who were dissatisfied with the zamindari's policies, and if there were any measures being taken to address their grievances.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was starting to think that Nikhil's warnings were nothing more than an excuse to gain more influence over the zamindari's policies, and that his motives were as transparent as a muddy pond.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his carefree attitude would only lead to disaster and that the zamindari's very existence was at stake

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Nikhil and asked what measures he had taken to ensure the zamindari's relations with the local Mussulmans were peaceful and prosperous.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had ever considered that the real threat to the zamindari's existence was not the Mussulmans, but his own ineptitude in governing the estate

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that such frivolous remarks were unbecoming of a zamindar, and that he would do well to focus on the gravity of the situation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if he had given any thought to the economic implications of the potential conflict with the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he was still waiting for some concrete evidence of these alleged threats, and that until then, he would continue to govern his estate with the flair and panache that had made his ancestors great

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip was being reckless in downplaying the threat, and that his own experience with the local Mussulmans had shown him the gravity of the situation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil how he proposed they handle the potential conflict, given the limited resources of the zamindari.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
